milestone: Hardening the Vela adapter/decode path after the public v0.2.0 devnet run — the multi-party AND single-party poll-to-terminal paths both fail closed against an execution failure being persisted as a constitutional determination.
problem: RES-2026-09-14-VELA-DEVNET-FUEL-ERRORCODE-MASKED-DISPOSITION-001 recorded a DIAGNOSTIC discipline (inspect the raw errorCode before trusting a decoded disposition). Following that finding through to the codebase's PRODUCTION consumers revealed the underlying architectural gap was real and unmitigated in two places: (1) services/vela/velaUnderwritingProjection.ts's pollMultiPartyDispositionToTerminal called getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition, which collapses an execution failure (Vela Executor errorCode !== 0) into the SAME string 'UNRESOLVED' a genuine guest-computed refusal produces — and the underwriting projection function then fed that string straight into provider.quoteForVerdict() and persisted it in an activity receipt and Golden Cycle telemetry, indistinguishable from a real constitutional UNRESOLVED. (2) services/factor/factorConfidentialWorkload.ts's pollToTerminal loop only checked `status.state === 'OBSERVING'` to decide whether to keep polling, and fell straight through to persistEvidence() (writing a factor_evidence_items row used as Aegis admission evidence) on ANY other terminal state INCLUDING 'FAILED' — with no check at all.
observedFailure: Neither production call path had ever been exercised with a real execution failure before the public devnet run — both were unit-tested only against errorCode: 0 and, in the single-party case, a directly-inspected getProjectionStatus/getProjectionEvidence call (tests/vela-confidential-projection-provider.test.ts's own FAILED test), never through pollToTerminal + persistEvidence together.
rootCauses: getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition's contract (add a coarse, three-valued-or-null return, collapsing EXECUTION_FAILED into 'UNRESOLVED') is correct for a caller that only needs the coarse disposition and treats both cases as fail-closed-equivalent — but it was the ONLY entry point the multi-party substrate exposed, so a caller that needed to persist evidence had no richer alternative to reach for.

factorConfidentialWorkload.ts's pollToTerminal was written to guard only against the 'stuck in OBSERVING forever' failure mode (the poll-timeout case) and never against the 'terminated as FAILED' case — a narrower guard than the function's own name/purpose implied.
resolution: Added VelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome (services/vela/velaMultiPartyProjection.ts) — a discriminated union ({status:'PENDING'} | {status:'EXECUTION_FAILED', errorCode, errorMsg} | {status:'RESOLVED', disposition}) and getVelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome(), the new preferred entry point for any caller that will persist the result. getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition is UNCHANGED and kept for existing callers that already treat failure/UNRESOLVED as equivalent on purpose — it now delegates to the new function internally, with identical external behaviour.

Updated velaUnderwritingProjection.ts's pollMultiPartyDispositionToTerminal to use getVelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome and THROW distinctly (naming the raw errorCode/errorMsg) on EXECUTION_FAILED, before any quote/receipt/telemetry call — mirroring the function's own existing poll-timeout throw.

Added optional executionErrorCode/executionErrorMessage fields to ConfidentialProjectionStatus (types/confidentialProjection.ts), populated by VelaConfidentialProjectionProvider.getProjectionStatus's existing FAILED branch (services/vela/velaProjectionProvider.ts) — additive, present ONLY alongside state:'FAILED'.

Updated factorConfidentialWorkload.ts's pollToTerminal to check status.state === 'FAILED' after the existing OBSERVING loop and throw distinctly (naming the errorCode when present) BEFORE either of its two call sites (runAdmissionPacketPolicyEvaluation, resumeAdmissionPacketPolicyEvaluation) can reach persistEvidence — one shared fix protects both callers.

Updated scripts/vela/public-devnet-smoke.ts's own diagnostics to use the new outcome function (pollOutcome helper), so the tool that surfaced this defect no longer requires manual errorCode inspection to avoid being misled by it again.

Added targeted tests: 6 new cases in tests/vela-multi-party-projection.test.ts (PENDING/EXECUTION_FAILED/RESOLVED, legacy-disposition-unchanged, no-bypass-possible), 3 new cases in tests/vela-underwriting-projection.test.ts (throws with errorCode, never calls provider/receipt/telemetry on failure, genuine runs unaffected), 2 new cases in tests/factor-vela-confidential-workload.test.ts (single-party equivalent), 1 new case in tests/vela-confidential-projection-provider.test.ts (new fields populated only on FAILED).
rejectedApproaches: Changing getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition's own return contract to surface the distinction directly (e.g. a 4th sentinel value) — rejected because existing callers/tests rely on its exact three-valued-or-null contract, and CLAUDE.md's discipline is to extend by composition, not by changing a stable contract's meaning out from under callers who chose it deliberately.

Broadening ConfidentialProjectionDisposition itself with a 4th 'EXECUTION_FAILED' value — rejected as a much larger, more invasive schema change (touches every consumer of the 3-valued disposition enum across the single- and multi-party substrates, receipts, telemetry, and the composition gate) for a distinction that is fully addressable at the poll-to-terminal layer, which is the one layer that actually decides whether to persist anything.

Silently persisting execution-failure evidence with a special marker field instead of throwing — rejected: there is no legitimate quote, receipt, or telemetry record to produce for a request the guest never actually executed; refusing to produce one at all (mirroring the existing poll-timeout throw) is the more honest, and more minimal, fix.
canaries: tests/vela-underwriting-projection.test.ts — describe('Execution Failure Non-Equivalence — a Vela execution failure is never persisted as a constitutional determination')
tests/factor-vela-confidential-workload.test.ts — describe('Execution Failure Non-Equivalence — a Vela execution failure is never persisted as constitutional evidence')
tests/vela-confidential-projection-provider.test.ts — 'an Executor-side failure is UNRESOLVED, never UNACCEPTABLE' (extended) and the new 'never carries executionErrorCode/executionErrorMessage' case
